<PubmedArticle><MedlineCitation Status="PubMed-not-MEDLINE" Owner="NLM"><PMID Version="1">38145207</PMID><DateRevised><Year>2023</Year><Month>12</Month><Day>25</Day></DateRevised><Article PubModel="Electronic-eCollection"><Journal><ISSN IssnType="Print">1663-3563</ISSN><JournalIssue CitedMedium="Print"><Volume>15</Volume><PubDate><Year>2023</Year></PubDate></JournalIssue><Title>Frontiers in synaptic neuroscience</Title><ISOAbbreviation>Front Synaptic Neurosci</ISOAbbreviation></Journal><ArticleTitle>Synaptic plasticity through a naturalistic lens.</ArticleTitle><Pagination><StartPage>1250753</StartPage><MedlinePgn>1250753</MedlinePgn></Pagination><ELocationID EIdType="pii" ValidYN="Y">1250753</ELocationID><ELocationID EIdType="doi" ValidYN="Y">10.3389/fnsyn.2023.1250753</ELocationID><Abstract><AbstractText>From the myriad of studies on neuronal plasticity, investigating its underlying molecular mechanisms up to its behavioral relevance, a very complex landscape has emerged. Recent efforts have been achieved toward more naturalistic investigations as an attempt to better capture the synaptic plasticity underpinning of learning and memory, which has been fostered by the development of <i>in vivo</i> electrophysiological and imaging tools. In this review, we examine these naturalistic investigations, by devoting a first part to synaptic plasticity rules issued from naturalistic <i>in vivo</i>-like activity patterns. We next give an overview of the novel tools, which enable an increased spatio-temporal specificity for detecting and manipulating plasticity expressed at individual spines up to neuronal circuit level during behavior. Finally, we put particular emphasis on works considering brain-body communication loops and macroscale contributors to synaptic plasticity, such as body internal states and brain energy metabolism.</AbstractText><CopyrightInformation>Copyright &#xa9; 2023 Piette, Gervasi and Venance.</CopyrightInformation></Abstract><AuthorList CompleteYN="Y"><Author
